title: All Souls Novena
description: A novena prayed for the holy souls in purgatory, traditionally from October 24 to November 1, culminating on All Souls Day (November 2). This powerful novena honors the Church's teaching on purgatory and offers spiritual assistance to the faithful departed who are being purified before entering heaven. The faithful who devoutly pray this novena help the holy souls reach their eternal home.
intention: For the holy souls in purgatory, that they may be purified and enter into the joy of heaven; for all the faithful departed, especially those who have no one to pray for them
instructions: This novena is traditionally prayed from October 24 to November 1, in preparation for All Souls Day (November 2). Begin each day with the Sign of the Cross. Include your personal intentions, especially naming deceased loved ones you wish to pray for. This novena may also be prayed at any time for the holy souls. Consider offering your daily Mass, Rosary, and sacrifices for the souls in purgatory during this novena.
background_info: The Church has always prayed for the dead, as seen in 2 Maccabees 12:46: 'It is therefore a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead, that they may be loosed from sins.' Purgatory is the state of purification for those who die in God's grace but need to be purified of the temporal effects of sin before entering heaven. The holy souls cannot help themselves but depend on our prayers, Masses, and sacrifices. St. Thomas Aquinas taught that the souls in purgatory are at peace, knowing they will see God. This novena includes the traditional prayers: Eternal Rest, De Profundis (Psalm 130), and prayers for final perseverance.

days.title: Day 1: The Reality of Purgatory
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal Rest

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the souls of the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, King of glory, we commend to Your mercy the holy souls in purgatory, especially those who have died in Your grace but still await the fullness of Your presence.

You have taught us that nothing unclean shall enter heaven. For those who die in Your friendship but still bear the stains of sin or the temporal punishment due to sin, You have provided a place of purification. Purgatory is Your mercy, for it is the antechamber of heaven where souls are made ready to see Your face.

Today we pray for all the holy souls. We unite our prayers with the sufferings of Your Passion, that they may be speedily delivered from their pains and admitted to the glory of Your presence.

We offer You the Most Holy Sacrifice of the Mass, the merits of the Blessed Virgin Mary, of all the angels and saints, and of all good Christians, and we ask that You apply these merits to the souls in purgatory, especially those most abandoned and forgotten.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be

Requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine, et lux perpetua luceat eis. Requiescant in pace. Amen.
days.closing_prayer:
O merciful Jesus, who desires not the death of sinners but that they should be converted and live, we ask You to look with pity on the holy souls in purgatory. Shorten their time of trial, and bring them soon to the vision of Your glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

May the divine assistance remain always with us, and may the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.reflection: Purgatory is a doctrine of hope and mercy. It testifies to God's perfect justice and His abundant love. No one in purgatory will ever be lost - they are all assured of heaven. They are called 'holy souls' because they died in God's grace. Their suffering is the pain of longing for God, and their greatest desire is to be purified so they can see Him face to face. To pray for the dead is an act of mercy and charity that binds the Church on earth to the Church suffering.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, have mercy on the souls in purgatory, especially those who have no one to pray for them. I offer my prayers, works, joys, and sufferings of this day for their relief. [Name any deceased loved ones you wish to pray for]
days.scripture: "It is therefore a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead, that they may be loosed from sins." - 2 Maccabees 12:46

days.title: Day 2: The Suffering of the Holy Souls
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

De Profundis (Psalm 130)

Out of the depths I cry to you, O Lord;
Lord, hear my voice!
Let your ears be attentive
To the voice of my supplications!

If you, O Lord, should mark iniquities,
Lord, who could stand?
But there is forgiveness with you,
That you may be feared.

I wait for the Lord, my soul waits,
And in his word I hope;
My soul waits for the Lord
More than watchmen for the morning,
More than watchmen for the morning.

O Israel, hope in the Lord!
For with the Lord there is steadfast love,
And with him is plenteous redemption.
And he will redeem Israel
From all his iniquities.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, we contemplate today the sufferings of the holy souls in purgatory. Though their sufferings are great, they bear them with patience, resignation, and even joy, for they know these pains are the means by which they are being purified for heaven.

The greatest suffering of the holy souls is not the fire that purifies them, but the pain of being separated from God, whom they love above all things. They see Your beauty and goodness from a distance and long to be with You. This longing is both their greatest pain and their greatest hope.

St. Catherine of Genoa taught that the souls in purgatory are so conformed to God's will that they would rather stay in purgatory until the last day than leave one spot of sin unforgiven. Their union with Your will is perfect, even in their suffering.

We offer our prayers today that their purification may be speeded, that they may soon see Your face and enter into Your joy.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: O Jesus, who suffered on the cross for our salvation, we offer You the pains of the holy souls in purgatory, united to Your own Passion. May Your merits shorten their time of purification. Bring them soon to be with You in paradise. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: The suffering of purgatory is both a pain and a joy. The souls experience the 'pain of loss' - separation from God - which is the greatest suffering possible for a soul that loves Him. But they also experience the 'pain of sense' - the purifying fire that burns away all attachment to sin. What sustains them is the certainty of heaven, the knowledge that their suffering is temporary and purposeful, and their perfect conformity to God's will.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, I offer all my prayers and sufferings of this day for the holy souls in purgatory, that their pains may be shortened and that they may soon see Your face. [Name deceased loved ones]
days.scripture: "Each one's work will become manifest, for the Day will disclose it, because it will be revealed with fire, and the fire will test what sort of work each one has done." - 1 Corinthians 3:13

days.title: Day 3: The Mercy of Purgatory
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the souls of the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, we contemplate today the great mercy that is purgatory. What we call a place of punishment is in truth a place of mercy, for without this purification, many souls could never enter heaven.

Your justice demands that nothing defiled enter Your presence, yet Your mercy provides a way for those who die in Your friendship but not yet perfected. Purgatory is the meeting place of Your justice and Your mercy - justice requires purification, but mercy supplies the means.

The holy souls know this and are grateful. They do not complain, but accept their purification with joy, knowing that when it is complete, they will see You face to face. They are truly blessed, for they have died in Your grace and their salvation is assured.

Thank You, Lord, for the gift of purgatory. It is a testimony to Your love that You do not give up on us, even after death, but provide a way for us to be made perfect.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be

Prayer for the Grace of Final Perseverance

O my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, through Your bitter passion and death, give me the grace of final perseverance. Let me die in Your grace, and if I must suffer in purgatory, accept my sufferings in union with Yours. I offer all my sufferings for the holy souls there. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: O God of infinite mercy, we thank You for the gift of purgatory, where Your justice and mercy embrace. Hasten the purification of the holy souls, and bring them soon to the wedding feast of heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: Purgatory reveals the depths of God's mercy. He does not desire that any should perish but that all should come to repentance. For those who die in His friendship but with the stains of sin, He provides a final purification that is itself a gift. The souls in purgatory are not being punished in spite of God's love; they are being purified because of it. Every soul in purgatory will one day be a saint in heaven.
days.intention_prayer: Merciful Jesus, I pray for the holy souls in purgatory, especially those who died without the Last Sacraments. Give them the peace of Your mercy. [Name deceased loved ones]
days.scripture: "Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy." - Matthew 5:7

days.title: Day 4: The Poor Souls Most Abandoned
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the souls of the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, today we pray especially for the most abandoned souls in purgatory - those who have no one to pray for them, those who are forgotten by the living, and those who have been longest in their purification.

There are souls whose families have died, or whose loved ones have forgotten them, or who never had anyone to remember them. These poor souls long for the prayers that will release them, but they wait in silence. Today, we remember them.

We remember also those souls who were most attached to the things of this world, whose purification is longest and most intense. They need our prayers all the more.

St. Gertrude the Great had a vision of many souls being released from purgatory when she prayed. You revealed to her a special prayer: 'Eternal Father, I offer You the Most Precious Blood of Your Divine Son, Jesus, in union with all the Masses said throughout the world today, for all the holy souls in purgatory, for sinners everywhere, for sinners in the universal church, those in my own home and within my family. Amen.' You promised that 1,000 souls would be released each time this prayer is prayed devoutly.

Eternal Father, I offer You the Most Precious Blood of Your Divine Son, Jesus, in union with all the Masses said throughout the world today, for all the holy souls in purgatory, for sinners everywhere, for sinners in the universal church, those in my own home and within my family. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer: O Jesus, who said 'I was a stranger and you welcomed me,' we pray for those souls who are strangers to the living, with no one to remember them. May our prayers today bring them comfort and speed their entry into heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: Many souls in purgatory are truly 'poor' - not because they lack God's love, but because they lack our prayers. Time passes, families forget, and some souls remain unknown to any living person. Yet they wait, hoping that someone, somewhere, will remember them. This is why the Church encourages us to pray generically for 'all the faithful departed' - so that no soul is forgotten.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, I pray today for the most abandoned souls in purgatory - those with no one to pray for them. May this prayer bring them relief and hasten their entrance into Your kingdom. [Include your own deceased loved ones]
days.scripture: "I was a stranger and you welcomed me... Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brethren, you did it to me." - Matthew 25:35, 40

days.title: Day 5: The Mass and the Holy Souls
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the souls of the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, who offers Yourself perpetually to the Father in the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass, we remember today that the Mass is the most powerful prayer we can offer for the holy souls.

In every Mass, You renew Your sacrifice on the cross, which is of infinite value and merit. When a Mass is offered for a soul in purgatory, Your sacrifice is applied to that soul in a special way. The saints tell us that one Mass offered for a soul can release them entirely from purgatory.

Padre Pio said that more souls of the dead go to heaven through the Mass than through the prayers of the saints, because the Mass is the sacrifice of Christ Himself, applied to them.

We pray today for all the souls who have had Masses offered for them, and for all the souls who need Masses. May the Most Holy Sacrifice of the altar speed their purification and bring them soon to Your presence.

O Holy Jesus, through Your Precious Blood shed on the Cross and re-presented on our altars, have mercy on the souls in purgatory. Let the fruits of Your sacrifice be applied to them, that they may soon be with You forever.

We offer all the Masses being celebrated today throughout the world for the holy souls in purgatory.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer: O Jesus, High Priest and Victim, we commend to You the holy souls in purgatory, especially those for whom Masses are being offered today. May the fruits of Your sacrifice bring them quickly to Your heavenly banquet. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: The Mass is the greatest prayer we can offer for the dead because it is the sacrifice of Christ Himself. Christ's sacrifice has infinite merit, and when we offer a Mass for a soul, we are asking that the merits of His death be applied to that particular soul. The Church has always practiced offering Masses for the dead, as testified by inscriptions in the catacombs. The Mass reduces the time of purification in purgatory in a way that no other prayer can.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, I offer all the Masses being celebrated today for the holy souls in purgatory. May the Precious Blood of Jesus bring them relief and release. I also pray for [name deceased loved ones].
days.scripture: "Therefore he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, since a death has occurred which redeems them from the transgressions under the first covenant." - Hebrews 9:15

days.title: Day 6: Our Lady and the Holy Souls
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Hail, Holy Queen

Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy,
Hail, our life, our sweetness, and our hope.
To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve;
To thee do we send up our sighs,
Mourning and weeping in this valley of tears.
Turn, then, most gracious advocate,
Thine eyes of mercy toward us,
And after this our exile, show unto us
The blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Pray for us, O holy Mother of God,
That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, today we invoke the intercession of Your Blessed Mother for the holy souls in purgatory. Mary, the Mother of the Church, cares for all her children, including those being purified in purgatory.

The saints tell us that Mary frequently visits the holy souls, bringing them comfort and consolation. St. Bridget of Sweden recorded a revelation in which Our Lord told her: 'My Mother, as a most pitiful mother, frequently visits the holy souls and consoles them.'

Mary is called the 'Gate of Heaven' because through her, Jesus came into the world. She is also the one who helps open heaven's gate for the holy souls. Her intercession is powerful, for she is the Mother of the Judge and the Queen of Heaven.

We ask Mary, conceived without sin, to obtain from her Son the grace of speedy delivery for the souls in purgatory. May she who stood at the foot of the cross, where her Son purchased our redemption, now stand at the threshold of heaven to welcome the souls being purified.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen. (3 times)

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer: O Mary, Queen of the Holy Souls, we entrust to your maternal heart all the faithful departed. You who are the Mother of compassion, obtain from your Son the grace of release for those still in purgatory. Welcome them into your home in heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: Mary has a special relationship with the souls in purgatory. As Mother of the Church, she cares for the suffering souls as for her own children. Many saints have seen visions of Mary visiting purgatory, bringing comfort and relief. St. Alphonsus Liguori wrote: 'Mary not only assists her devout servants in purgatory, but even the souls of those who have been devout to her in life receive great relief from her.' Her intercession is especially powerful because she is the Mother of the Judge Himself.
days.intention_prayer: Mary, Mother of Mercy, I entrust to you all the holy souls in purgatory, especially [name deceased loved ones]. Obtain for them the grace of eternal life. Pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.
days.scripture: "Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother... When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing nearby, he said to his mother, 'Woman, behold, your son!' Then he said to the disciple, 'Behold, your mother!'" - John 19:25-26

days.title: Day 7: The Saints and the Holy Souls
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the souls of the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

Litany of the Saints (excerpt)

Saints of God, come to their aid.
Come to their aid, all you holy angels and archangels.
Come to their aid, all you holy patriarchs and prophets.
Come to their aid, all you holy apostles and evangelists.
Come to their aid, all you holy martyrs and confessors.
Come to their aid, all you holy virgins and widows.
Come to their aid, all you holy men and women, saints of God.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, today we invoke the intercession of all the saints for the holy souls in purgatory. The saints are Your friends who now see You face to face. They intercede constantly for those still on the journey, including those being purified in purgatory.

The saints, especially those who were particularly devoted to praying for the dead during their earthly lives, continue to intercede for the holy souls. St. Nicholas of Tolentino, known as the 'saint of the holy souls,' was granted a vision of souls being released from purgatory through his prayers and sacrifices.

St. Monica, on her deathbed, asked her son Augustine: 'Lay this body anywhere... Only this I ask of you: remember me at the altar of the Lord wherever you may be.' She trusted in the prayers of the living to speed her purification.

St. Catherine of Genoa, who had mystical visions of purgatory, wrote that the souls there cannot pray for themselves, but they can pray for us on earth. In gratitude for our prayers, they intercede for us before God. What a communion of charity!

We ask all the saints to intercede for the holy souls: all you holy men and women, pray for them.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be

St. Nicholas of Tolentino, patron of the holy souls, pray for them.
St. Monica, who trusted in the prayers of the faithful, pray for them.
All you saints of God, pray for them.
days.closing_prayer: O Lord, hear the prayers of Your saints for the holy souls in purgatory. United with them in the communion of saints, we ask that the souls we pray for today may soon join You and all the saints in heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: The communion of saints includes not only the saints in heaven but also the souls in purgatory and us on earth. We are all connected in Christ. The saints in heaven intercede for us and for the souls in purgatory. The souls in purgatory cannot help themselves, but they can pray for us - and they do, with great fervor, thanking us for our prayers. When they reach heaven, they will be grateful intercessors for those who helped them on their way.
days.intention_prayer: All you saints of God, I ask your intercession for the holy souls in purgatory, especially [name deceased loved ones]. Obtain for them the vision of God. St. Nicholas of Tolentino, St. Monica, and all holy souls' patrons, pray for us.
days.scripture: "Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us." - Hebrews 12:1

days.title: Day 8: The Suffering Church and Our Duty
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the souls of the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, today we reflect on our duty to pray for the souls in purgatory. The Church teaches that we, the Church Militant on earth, have a serious obligation to assist the Church Suffering in purgatory.

These souls are our brothers and sisters in Christ. They cannot help themselves - they cannot pray for their own release, nor can they perform the good works that would shorten their time of purification. They depend entirely on us, the Church on earth.

St. Thomas Aquinas taught that praying for the dead is an act of charity more pleasing to God than praying for the living, because the dead have no other way to help themselves. St. John Chrysostom said: 'It is not without reason that the Apostles ordained a remembrance of the dead in the sacred mysteries. They know that much gain results to them, much benefit.'

We, who one day may be in purgatory ourselves, should pray for the dead with generosity. For as we show mercy to them, so will mercy be shown to us. The measure we give will be the measure we receive.

We commit today to make prayer for the dead a regular practice: at Mass, in our daily prayers, and when we think of our deceased loved ones. We will offer our sufferings, our sacrifices, and our indulgences for them.

Prayer of Commitment

Lord Jesus, I commit to praying regularly for the holy souls in purgatory. I will remember them at Mass, in my Rosary, and in my daily prayers. I offer my sufferings for them. And when I die, I pray that the prayers of the faithful will speed my own purification. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer: O Jesus, who taught us to love our neighbor, we recognize the holy souls as our suffering neighbors. May we never forget them, but bring them faithfully to You in prayer, that they may pray for us when they reach Your presence. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: Praying for the dead is a spiritual work of mercy and a serious duty. The deceased can no longer pray for themselves, offer indulgences, or have Masses said; they rely entirely on the living. St. John Vianney said: 'We must pray for the poor souls. If we only knew what they suffer, we would not cease praying for them.' The holy souls are our friends waiting to welcome us into heaven; what we do for them, Christ counts as done for Himself.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, forgive me for the times I have forgotten the holy souls. I commit to praying for them faithfully. Have mercy on [name deceased loved ones] and all the faithful departed. Amen.
days.scripture: "Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, O you my friends, for the hand of God has touched me!" - Job 19:21

days.title: Day 9: The Joy of Heaven - The Holy Souls Released
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Te Deum (excerpt)

We praise you, O God;
We acclaim you as Lord;
All the earth worships you,
You, the eternal Father.
To you all angels, all the powers of heaven,
Cherubim and Seraphim, sing in endless praise:
Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of hosts.
Heaven and earth are full of your glory.

Come, let us worship the Lord, the King of glory.
Come, let us adore the Lord, the King of glory.
Come, let us adore the Lord, the eternal King, the Savior of the world.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, on this final day of our novena, we contemplate with joy the destiny of the holy souls: the vision of Your face in heaven.

When their purification is complete, the holy souls are released from purgatory and welcomed into Your presence. What a moment of joy that must be! They who have longed for You, suffered in separation from You, now see You face to face. All their pain is forgotten in an instant, replaced by the infinite joy of Your presence.

St. Catherine of Genoa wrote: 'No happiness can be found worthy to be compared with that of a soul in purgatory as she sees her purification approaching its end.' How much greater, then, is the happiness when it actually ends!

We pray today that through this novena, many souls have been released from purgatory. We offer thanks for all the souls who, because of our prayers, now see Your face. We entrust to You all those still waiting, that they too may soon be with You.

And we pray for ourselves: that we may live so as to avoid purgatory, or at least to shorten our time there. Keep us from serious sin, give us the grace of final perseverance, and in Your mercy, bring us one day to Your heavenly kingdom, where we will join all the angels and saints in praising You forever.

Prayer of Thanksgiving

We give thanks, O Lord, for all the souls who through this novena have been released from purgatory. We rejoice with them and with all the saints. May they now intercede for us before Your throne. And may we one day join them in Your eternal kingdom. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer:
O Jesus, King of glory, we entrust to You all the holy souls for whom we have prayed during this novena. May they now see Your face and share in Your eternal joy. Give us the grace to join them one day, praising You forever with all the angels and saints. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

May they rest in peace. Amen.

May their souls and the souls of all the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.reflection: The holy souls in purgatory will all, without exception, reach heaven. Their salvation is certain; they are simply being prepared for the Beatific Vision. When they finally see God face to face, all their suffering will be forgotten in an instant. They will be reunited with loved ones, welcomed by the saints, and embraced by God Himself. This is our hope - and it is also our calling. We too are destined for heaven, if we remain faithful. Let us pray for the dead with confidence, knowing that one day we will meet them in glory.
days.intention_prayer: Almighty God, I commend to You all the faithful departed for whom I have prayed during this novena, especially [name deceased loved ones]. May they rest in peace and rise in glory. And grant that I may live so as to merit eternal life with You and all the saints. Amen.
days.scripture: "Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth... and I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, 'Behold, the dwelling of God is with men. He will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself will be with them; he will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning nor crying nor pain any more, for the former things have passed away.'" - Revelation 21:1-4

source: Ancient tradition of the Church, based on the constant practice of praying for the faithful departed
notes: This novena is traditionally prayed October 24 - November 1, in preparation for All Souls Day on November 2. The Church has prayed for the dead since Apostolic times (2 Maccabees 12:46, 2 Timothy 1:16-18). Purgatory is the state of purification for those who die in God's grace but are not yet fully purified. The holy souls cannot pray for themselves but depend on the prayers, Masses, and sacrifices of the living. Key prayers used include the Requiem Aeternam (Eternal Rest), De Profundis (Psalm 130), and the Prayer of St. Gertrude. Saints particularly devoted to the holy souls include St. Nicholas of Tolentino (patron of holy souls), St. Catherine of Genoa (mystic of purgatory), and St. Padre Pio. Offering Masses for the dead is the most efficacious way to help them. The Church grants indulgences applicable to the souls in purgatory under the usual conditions during the octave of All Souls (November 1-8).
